project.name: Quanta Epidemic Resources Allocation
project.domain: Healthcare, Epidemic Response, Quantum Optimization, Quantum AI
project.objective: Build a complete hybrid classical-quantum decision-support system that analyzes epidemic risk and mobility/contact networks, evaluates possible facility locations, and uses QAOA with Qiskit/Aer to select the best combination of exactly five facilities from a larger candidate set.

important_instructions.instruction: Build the project as a fully working prototype, not a collection of placeholder screens or mock buttons.
The complete pipeline must work end-to-end: epidemic data → ML risk analysis → network analysis → facility analysis → QUBO → QAOA → facility selection → evaluation → visualization.
The ML model must NOT directly select the final facilities. ML is used to estimate epidemic risk and produce information that becomes an input to the optimization problem.
The quantum component must genuinely use Qiskit and Qiskit Aer to execute QAOA. Do not simulate QAOA using an ordinary classical optimization algorithm while presenting it as quantum.
Do not claim quantum advantage, quantum speedup, or superiority over classical optimization unless the implemented experiments actually demonstrate it.
Use synthetic data by default so that the application can run without external datasets. Design the data layer so a public dataset can be substituted later.
Do not use arbitrary 4-bit identifiers as the QAOA decision encoding. Facility IDs are metadata. Use one binary decision variable per candidate facility in the optimization model.
Keep the project modular and production-quality even though it is a hackathon prototype.

problem_definition.description: During an epidemic, authorities may have many possible locations but limited resources. For example, there may be 20 candidate locations, while only 5 testing, vaccination, isolation, or other epidemic-response facilities can be deployed.
problem_definition.goal: Select exactly five facilities that provide the best overall epidemic response considering risk, population, mobility/contact network, accessibility, travel distance, facility capacity, and deployment cost.
problem_definition.key_question: Given all epidemic and facility information and a strict limit of five facilities, which combination of locations provides the best overall coverage and resource allocation?

system_flow.stage: Load or generate: epidemic data, population data, mobility/contact data, candidate facility data.
Train or load a classical ML model that estimates epidemic risk for each area. Output a normalized risk score between 0 and 1.

Construct a weighted contact/mobility graph. Nodes represent geographical areas. Edges represent movement/contact. Edge weights represent interaction intensity. Calculate useful graph metrics such as weighted degree, centrality, neighboring population, and risk-weighted connectivity.
Calculate the usefulness of every facility using: risk, population, network connectivity, accessibility, distance, capacity, deployment cost.

Remove facilities that are clearly infeasible according to configurable rules such as insufficient capacity, excessive cost, invalid location, or other hard constraints. Do not confuse candidate filtering with final optimization.
Create one binary decision variable x_i for every eligible facility. x_i = 1 means facility i is selected. x_i = 0 means facility i is not selected.
Convert the QUBO into the appropriate quantum cost representation and execute QAOA using Qiskit and Qiskit Aer.
Convert the measured bitstring into facility IDs. Identify the best feasible solution.
Solve the exact same optimization problem using a classical MILP optimizer.
Compare QAOA and classical results using identical inputs, objectives, weights, and constraints.
Display all facilities, candidate facilities, QAOA processing, selected facilities, coverage, network effects, and comparison metrics.

machine_learning.models: Random Forest or Gradient Boosting initially.
machine_learning.fallback: If reliable labeled epidemic data is unavailable, implement a transparent mathematical risk-scoring model and clearly label it as a risk model rather than ML.

classical_optimization.purpose: Strong classical baseline for comparison with QAOA.

machine_learning_module.purpose: Estimate the epidemic risk of each geographical area.
machine_learning_module.input_features: population, population_density, current_cases, recent_case_growth, mobility_index, contact_intensity
machine_learning_module.example: Area A01 → 0.91 → High Risk Area A02 → 0.47 → Medium Risk Area A03 → 0.18 → Low Risk
machine_learning_module.important: Risk prediction and facility optimization are separate modules.

network_module.representation: Represent the city as a weighted graph.
network_module.purpose: Ensure the optimizer considers how epidemic risk propagates through connected areas rather than only selecting locations with high local risk.

facility_optimization.meaning: x_i = 1 → facility i is selected. x_i = 0 → facility i is not selected.
facility_optimization.configurable_weights: risk_weight, population_weight, network_weight, accessibility_weight, distance_weight, cost_weight

qubo.definition: QUBO means Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization. It is the mathematical representation used before applying QAOA. QUBO itself is not quantum annealing.
qubo.conceptual_objective: Q(x) = -Coverage(x) + λ1 * TravelCost(x) + λ2 * DeploymentCost(x) + P * (Σx_i - 5)^2
qubo.requirements: Generate the QUBO programmatically from the current scenario. Do not hard-code a sample matrix. Make all major weights configurable. Log the final QUBO size and relevant coefficients for experiments.

qaoa.flow: QUBO → Ising-compatible cost representation → QAOA circuit → parameter optimization → measurement → bitstring samples → best feasible solution
qaoa.display_results: qaoa_depth, beta_parameters, gamma_parameters, measurement_counts, probability_distribution, best_bitstring, objective_value
qaoa.simulation_strategy: Start with small candidate sets such as 8–12 facilities. Test 16 or larger only if simulator performance permits.
qaoa.feasibility: The application must verify that the final bitstring satisfies the exactly-five-facilities constraint. Use sufficiently strong penalty terms and/or select the best feasible sampled bitstring. Any repair strategy must be explicitly documented.

classical_baseline.requirements: Use exactly the same: input data, candidate facilities, objective, weights, constraints.
classical_baseline.metrics: objective_value, population_coverage, high_risk_coverage, average_travel_distance, maximum_travel_distance, deployment_cost, constraint_violations, runtime
classical_baseline.purpose: Establish a scientifically meaningful classical reference.

user_interface.design_goal: Make the UI feel like an epidemic-response command center. The interface must visually explain what happens from raw facilities to the final optimized facility set.

page.name: All Facilities
page.purpose: Show the complete initial problem before optimization.
page.show: every possible facility, location, capacity, deployment_cost, accessibility
page.map: Display all facilities as candidate markers. Display epidemic risk on surrounding areas.

page.name: Risk and Network
page.show: ML risk scores, risk categories, mobility/contact network, network metrics
page.visualization: High-risk areas should be visually distinct. Mobility/contact edges should be visible.

page.name: Candidate Facilities
page.purpose: Show the facilities that remain eligible after classical analysis.
page.important: Label these as Candidate/Eligible Facilities, not final selected facilities.
page.show: eligible facilities, filtered facilities, reason for filtering, facility scores

page.name: Optimization
page.controls: number_of_facilities = 5, risk_weight, population_weight, network_weight, accessibility_weight, distance_weight, cost_weight

page.name: Quantum QAOA
page.show: QAOA circuit information, number_of_qubits, QAOA_depth, beta_parameters, gamma_parameters, measurement_counts, probability_distribution, sampled_bitstrings, best_feasible_bitstring
page.mapping: Each bit corresponds to one eligible facility. Example: bit 1 → F01 bit 0 → F02 bit 1 → F03
page.visualization: Display a ranked bar chart of the most frequently measured bitstrings and highlight the best feasible solution.

page.name: Final Results
page.show: final five facilities, population coverage, high_risk_coverage, average_travel_distance, maximum_travel_distance, deployment_cost, objective_value, feasibility
page.map: Highlight the five final facilities. Show their service/coverage regions. Show covered and poorly covered high-risk areas.

visualization.main_map: The interactive map/network is the centerpiece of the application.
visualization.legend: High risk = red Medium risk = orange Low risk = green Candidate facility = circle Selected facility = highlighted/star marker Mobility/contact = weighted edge
visualization.required_visualizations: epidemic risk map, contact/mobility network, facility locations, candidate facilities, selected facilities, facility coverage, QAOA bitstring distribution, classical-vs-QAOA metrics
visualization.charts: facility risk ranking, population coverage comparison, high-risk coverage comparison, travel distance comparison, cost comparison, objective value comparison, QAOA bitstring frequency
visualization.interaction: Clicking a facility should display its details. Clicking an area should display epidemic and risk information. Selecting a final facility should show the areas it serves.

api.endpoint: Generate a reproducible synthetic epidemic scenario.
Construct and analyze the mobility/contact network.
Calculate facility metrics and candidate eligibility.
Generate the QUBO from the current optimization configuration.

sample_scenario.setup: Generate 20 geographical areas. Generate 15–20 candidate facilities. Require exactly 5 facilities to be selected.
sample_scenario.final_example: QAOA may produce a feasible solution such as: F03, F06, F10, F13, F15
sample_scenario.important: The example result must not be hard-coded. It must be calculated by the implemented optimization pipeline.

experiment_design.purpose: Evaluate how QAOA behaves as the facility-selection problem grows.
experiment_design.repeat: Run multiple random seeds where practical.
experiment_design.record: candidate_count, selected_count, qaoa_depth, qaoa_parameters, objective_value, best_feasible_solution, classical_objective, population_coverage, high_risk_coverage, travel_distance, cost, runtime
experiment_design.analysis: Calculate relative objective quality and feasibility. Clearly distinguish simulator runtime from actual quantum hardware runtime.

error_handling.requirement: Handle invalid data, missing fields, infeasible scenarios, QUBO construction errors, QAOA failures, simulator timeouts and API errors.
error_handling.ui: Show meaningful error messages instead of generic failures.
error_handling.loading: Display progress states for ML, network analysis, QUBO generation, classical optimization and QAOA.

reproducibility.requirements: Use configurable random seeds. Store scenario configuration. Store optimization weights. Store QAOA configuration. Store experiment results.
reproducibility.purpose: A judge should be able to run the same scenario and reproduce the displayed result.

hackathon_demo.step: Open the dashboard and show the epidemic situation.
Show all 15–20 possible facilities on the map.
Display high-risk areas and the mobility/contact network.
Show candidate/eligible facilities after feasibility analysis.
Set the required number of facilities to 5.
Display QAOA measurement probabilities and bitstrings.
Decode the best feasible bitstring into facility IDs.
Highlight the final five facilities on the map.
Show the areas covered by the selected facilities.
Explain the results honestly without claiming unsupported quantum advantage.

novelty.statement: Epidemic facility placement is an established classical optimization problem. The novelty of this prototype is not inventing facility placement itself.
novelty.contribution: The project combines classical epidemic-risk prediction and network analysis with a QUBO representation of constrained facility allocation and evaluates QAOA against a classical optimization baseline using the same problem.
novelty.points: Risk-aware facility optimization. Network-aware epidemic response. Separation of ML prediction and combinatorial optimization. QUBO formulation of the resource-allocation problem. QAOA implementation using Qiskit. Interactive visualization of quantum optimization. Classical-vs-quantum benchmarking.

future_scalability.current: Qiskit Aer simulator and small problem sizes.
future_scalability.future: Larger candidate networks. More complex resource allocation. Multiple facility types. Capacity allocation. Multiple epidemic scenarios. Real mobility datasets. Noise-aware experiments. Real quantum hardware when practical.
future_scalability.vision: The same mathematical optimization model should remain usable while replacing the simulator with future quantum hardware or other quantum optimization backends.

limitations.item: Simulator-based QAOA does not demonstrate real-world quantum advantage.
Small instances may be solved more effectively by classical methods.
QAOA performance depends on circuit depth, parameter optimization, problem structure and noise.
ML performance depends on the quality and realism of the training data.
Synthetic epidemic data demonstrates the software pipeline but does not validate real epidemiological predictions.
The system is a hackathon research prototype and decision-support tool, not a clinical or public-health directive.

development_order.phase: Create synthetic epidemic, area, network and facility data.
Implement facility coverage and feasibility calculations.
Add validation, reproducibility, error handling and experiment logging.
Polish the hackathon demo and presentation flow.

final_acceptance_criteria.criterion: The application can generate a complete epidemic scenario without requiring external data.
The ML/risk layer produces risk scores for areas.
A mobility/contact network is constructed and visualized.
All candidate facilities are visible before optimization.
Candidate/eligible facilities are displayed after classical analysis.
The system creates a real QUBO from the optimization configuration.
QAOA is genuinely executed through Qiskit/Aer.
The result is decoded into actual facility IDs.
Exactly five facilities are selected by default.
The same problem is solved using a classical MILP baseline.
Classical and QAOA results are compared using meaningful metrics.
The final five facilities are highlighted on an interactive map.
The entire process can be demonstrated live from input to final result.
The project does not make unsupported claims about quantum advantage.

project_build_prompt.final_project_statement: Quanta Epidemic Resources Allocation is a hybrid classical-quantum decision-support system that uses ML and network analytics to quantify epidemic risk, formulates limited-facility placement as a QUBO, and uses QAOA in Qiskit to identify a high-quality set of five facilities while benchmarking the result against classical optimization.
